lines: It names no group and no measurement, so it has one answer, not answers that vary.
``How many minutes is the bus ride for Millbrook students who ride the bus?''
Of the 60 Millbrook students surveyed, 24 --- or $40\%$ --- chose a decades theme,
$40\%$ is not ``most'' --- most means more than half. And the survey covers the 60
students asked, not all 720, so the sentence reaches beyond its own group.
A statistic --- it describes the 80-member sample, not all 1,200 members.
Time --- reaching every one of 1,200 members would take far too long.
$839$ --- it is off the frame of $001$--$720$, so skip it and read the next number.
Stratified. The grades differ a lot and a numbered list of all 720 exists, so draw
students at random from every grade, in proportion to grade size.
Advisory groups are built by grade, so each one is alike inside --- a stratum, not a
mix of the whole. Her 48 students are one or two grades, so the $62.5\%$ estimates
nothing about all 720. She may only say $62.5\%$ of those 48 students said yes.
A statistic. Draw the sample at random from the whole numbered list of 720, or
stratify by grade, so every grade can be chosen.
